newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece to tax interbank deal net income from Jan 1.
newsitem.headline: Greece to tax interbank deal net income from Jan 1.

text.p: Greece will tax net income from interbank deals, effective January 1, the finance ministry said in a statement.

"The government will proceed to taxing net income from (interbank deals) that will take place from January 1, 1997, in the interbank market in the same way that other bank income is treated tax wise," the finance ministry statement said.
To implement its decision, banks' 1997 income tax prepayment will be raised to 60 percent from 50 percent, it said.

Under current tax rules, banks' taxable profit is reduced by the amount of profit that is derived from tax-exempt income or income that enjoys special tax treatment -- for example, income from state debt paper and interest from interbank depos, it said.

"The different tax treatment of interest income from interbank deals, depos and loans, with the exception of mandatory deposits with the Bank of Greece, does not serve any specific purpose," the statement said.
The statement did not say at what rate interbank deals would be taxed or whether it would be a withholding tax. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
